title: How to undo a reconciliation in quickbooks online on Mac: steps and limits for accountants
metaTitle: How to undo a reconciliation in QuickBooks Online on Mac
description: Undo a full reconciliation in QuickBooks Online as the Primary Admin, unmark one transaction safely, and stop the next reopen. Steps for Mac users.
targetKeyword: how to undo a reconciliation in quickbooks online
intro: To undo a reconciliation in QuickBooks Online, sign in as the Primary Admin or ask your accountant to do it. Then go to Reconcile > History by account, click Undo in the Action column, and confirm. Intuit says the undo is irreversible and deletes the reports and attachments tied to that reconciliation, so save those first.
tldr: In QuickBooks Online, the full undo belongs to the Primary Admin. If you are not the Primary Admin, ask them or your accountant.
The path is Reconcile > History by account > Action column > Undo, then confirm. The undo cannot be reversed.
Undoing deletes the reconciliation reports and attachments, so export and save them before you click.
To fix one bad line, unmark that transaction and reconcile again. Removing a cleared line changes the next beginning balance.
A closing date with a password, set under Settings > Account and settings > Advanced > Accounting, stops most accidental reopens.

blocks.text: You undo a reconciliation when a closed month stops tying out. A bank line moves. A bill gets dated into a period that is already closed. A client sends a late correction. Then the balance is off, and someone has to reopen the month. This page covers the steps in QuickBooks Online on a Mac, what the undo deletes, and how to keep the fix small.
What undoing a reconciliation actually does

A reconciliation matches your register to a bank or credit card statement. When you finish, QuickBooks Online marks the matched lines as reconciled and keeps the statement balances for that month. Undoing the whole reconciliation removes that record for the month you pick. Check the register afterward to see which lines are open again.

Intuit's help article is blunt about the cost. Undoing a reconciliation is irreversible. It also permanently deletes the reports and attachments tied to that reconciliation. There is no undo for the undo. Treat the click as a one-way step, and prepare before you take it.
Who can undo the whole reconciliation

Intuit's article says to sign in as the Primary Admin, or to consult your accountant. If you are not the Primary Admin, do not guess your way through it. Send the admin the account, the month, and the reason for the undo. Ask them to run it or confirm it.

Intuit's article does not name a role for unmarking single transactions. It says to ask your accountant if you are unsure. Treat a single-line fix the same way. Check with the person who owns the books before you touch a closed month, even when your login lets you edit the register.

blocks.title: Check before you click
blocks.text: The undo is permanent and deletes attachments. Save the reconciliation report and every receipt linked to that month first. Do this even when the fix looks small.
Step by step: undo a full reconciliation on your Mac

These steps follow Intuit's help article for QuickBooks Online. Menu names can shift between updates, so match the labels on your screen to the steps below. If a label is missing, stop and check with the Primary Admin.

items: Open QuickBooks Online in your browser on your Mac, and sign in as the Primary Admin.
Save the reconciliation report and attachments for that month. The next section shows how.
Go to Reconcile > History by account.
Find the account and the reconciliation you want to undo.
In the Action column, click Undo.
Read the confirmation message. Look for the warning about deleted reports and attachments, then confirm.
Open the register for that account. Compare the open lines with the bank statement before you reconcile again.

blocks.text: After the undo, expect the register to look different. The reconciled marks for that month are gone. Write down the old statement balances now, because the old report will no longer show them.
Save what the undo deletes first

The undo deletes the reconciliation reports and attachments linked to that reconciliation. Open the reconciliation report for the month and save a PDF copy. Save each attached receipt or statement too. Name the folder with the account, the month, and the date you saved it. That gives you a clean trail if someone asks later.

Write down the statement ending balance and the balance shown on the report. You will compare the new reconciliation against those numbers. If the file holds client data, store the copy only where your firm allows. Follow your employer's rules on client records, even for a temporary copy on your desktop.
A common mistake is treating the undo as a reset. It is not a reset. It removes records. A copy saved before the click is the only way to get those records back.
Unmark one transaction instead of undoing everything

Often the problem is one line. A deposit cleared in the wrong month, or a payment got matched to the wrong bill. You do not need to undo the whole month for that. Unmarking one line is a smaller step, and it keeps the other matches in place.
Intuit's article describes the single-line fix. Work through it in the register, then reconcile again so the line lands where it belongs.

items: Open the register for the bank or credit card account.
Find the line you need to change.
Click its checkmark until it is blank. The status changes from Reconciled to Uncleared.
Reconcile the statement again and match the line to the right item.

blocks.title: The next month will move
blocks.text: Intuit warns that removing a cleared transaction changes the beginning balance for your next reconciliation. Open the next month before you close it, and compare its starting balance with the last statement.
What a reopened month costs your team

Reopens are not rare. In a 2022 survey by FloQast and the University of Georgia, 85% of 204 accounting and finance professionals said they reopened the books in at least one month of the past year to fix errors. Of all respondents, 49% said they did this in three or more months.

The same survey found that 81% had at least one month where the close disrupted their personal life. A reopen lands in the middle of other work. Plan for the time it takes, and tell the people around you when the close will run late.

Time is the other cost. A 2025 benchmark from Ledge, a vendor, reports that finance teams spend 20 to 50 hours a month on cash reconciliation. That survey covered 100 finance professionals. Use it as a rough benchmark, not a measure of your own team.

Put a dollar figure on that time with care. BLS puts the May 2025 median pay for accountants and auditors at $83,680 a year, or $40.23 an hour. At that base rate, 20 to 50 hours a month comes to about $805 to $2,012. This is an estimate of base wage time only. It leaves out benefits, overhead, and the client call.

blocks.text: Why reconciled months get reopened
The causes below are the usual ones. Each one has a fix in the sections that follow, and most are cheap to prevent before the next close.
Fixes you can use without buying anything
None of these fixes needs new software. They need a rule, a date, and a habit. Start with the closing date, because it blocks the most accidents for the least effort.
Set the closing date and check who can change it

The closing date is QuickBooks Online's main control against accidental reopens. Admins set it with a password. You find it at Settings > Account and settings > Advanced > Accounting. Only admins can change the date or the password.

Intuit advises reconciling up to the closing date first. Reconcile the month, then set the closing date. The Intuit article does not say whether closing a period changes the reconciled status of transactions. Confirm that with your admin before you promise a client that a closed month is frozen.

A closing date helps only when people know it. Post it in your team channel. Tell anyone who enters bills or bank rules about it. Check the Exceptions to Closing Date report after each close, because it lists changes made after the books were closed.
Desktop and Xero handle this differently

QuickBooks Desktop has a separate tool called Undo Last Reconciliation. Open Begin Reconciliation, select the account, then choose Undo Last Reconciliation. Desktop asks you to confirm a backup first. When it finishes, it shows Undo Previous Reconciliation has completed. It only reverses the most recent reconciliation, and Intuit's Desktop article gives no Mac-specific steps.

Xero works differently. This page does not cover Xero's steps in detail. Read Xero Central's article on fixing an incorrectly reconciled bank statement line before you change a Xero file. Confirm the steps match your version of Xero.
Plan the reopen across one week
A reopen goes faster when you split it into small steps. The plan below spreads the work across a week. That way the client and the next close do not wait on one long afternoon.
Where Lazur helps, and where it does not

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold a key and talk. Hold Option and Command (⌥ ⌘) to ask about anything on screen. Lazur sees your screen while you hold the shortcut, points at things, and answers out loud. It does not click buttons or change your books for you.

The best use here is guidance. Ask Lazur to walk you through the Reconcile steps. It guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. That helps when the menu names on your screen look different from this page. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Lazur can also help with the paperwork. Hold fn to dictate a clear reason for the reopen, and the text lands at your cursor in any app. Ask Lazur to draft the client email, then read it and send it yourself. For busy inboxes, see [Outlook for accountants on Mac](/for/accountants/outlook).
Two limits matter. Lazur runs only on macOS, and Windows is planned, not available. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for QuickBooks, and it has no partnership with Intuit.
Client data and your firm's rules

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your firm may still have rules on client data, and those rules come first.

If your firm does not allow client financial data in an AI tool, keep Lazur closed on those screens. Use Intuit's help articles and your own notes instead. Follow your employer's rules, even when a faster route exists.

faq.question: Can an accountant undo a reconciliation in QuickBooks Online?
faq.answer: Intuit's help article says the full undo is for the Primary Admin, or you can consult your accountant. If you are the accountant on the file, check your access level first. Single lines can be unmarked, but ask the books owner before you touch a closed month.

faq.question: Can I undo a reconciliation in QuickBooks Online and get it back?
faq.answer: No. Intuit states that undoing a reconciliation is irreversible. It also permanently deletes the reports and attachments linked to it. Save copies before you click Undo.

faq.question: What happens when I unmark one reconciled transaction?
faq.answer: Click the checkmark until it is blank, which changes the status from Reconciled to Uncleared. Then save and reconcile again. Removing a cleared transaction also changes the beginning balance for your next reconciliation.

faq.question: Does QuickBooks Desktop have the same undo?
faq.answer: QuickBooks Desktop has Undo Last Reconciliation. Choose it from Begin Reconciliation after you select the account, then confirm a backup. It only undoes the most recent reconciliation. Intuit's Desktop article gives no Mac-specific steps.

faq.question: How do I stop a closed month from reopening?
faq.answer: Set a closing date and password as an admin, under Settings > Account and settings > Advanced > Accounting. Reconcile up to the closing date first. Review the Exceptions to Closing Date report after each close.

faq.question: Does Xero work the same way?
faq.answer: Not in the same way. This page does not verify Xero's steps. Read Xero Central's article on fixing an incorrectly reconciled bank statement line before you change a Xero file.

faq.question: Can Lazur undo the reconciliation for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. You make the change yourself.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on client files?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules on client data first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

costs.title: Reports and attachments are gone
costs.text: The undo deletes the reconciliation reports and attachments for that month. If you did not save copies, the audit trail for that month is gone. Rebuilding a report later is not the same as keeping the original.

costs.title: Staff hours at base wage
costs.text: Ledge's benchmark of 20 to 50 hours a month, at the BLS median hourly wage of $40.23, comes to about $805 to $2,012 a month. This estimate uses base wage only, not a loaded cost.

costs.title: The next month can fail to tie
costs.text: Unmarking a cleared line changes the beginning balance for the next reconciliation. The next month may not tie, and the reopen spreads forward into a month you thought was finished.

costs.title: Stress and client trust
costs.text: In the 2022 survey, 81% said the close disrupted their personal life in at least one month. A reopen can also mean a second conversation with a client about numbers they already received.

causes.title: A late bank or card line
causes.text: Banks and card issuers post lines on their own schedule. A line can arrive dated in a month you already locked. Matching it into that month forces a reopen, even when the line itself is correct.

causes.title: A bill or payment dated into a closed month
causes.text: A transaction entered with an old date lands in a closed period. The closing date blocks this only when it is set and the team knows about it. Without that check, the error sits until someone finds the gap.

causes.title: A quick match made during a busy close
causes.text: Feed suggestions and quick matches get clicked fast when a deadline is close. A payment paired with the wrong bill can look fine until the balance is off. Nobody sees it until the month fails to tie.

causes.title: Side spreadsheets that disagree with the ledger
causes.text: Ledge's 2025 survey reports that 94% of finance teams use Excel in close. When a side tracker disagrees with the books, the fix often lands back in a month that is already closed.

causes.title: No owner for the reopen decision
causes.text: If nobody owns the reopen, the request turns into a favor between two people. The same month can then reopen again. Name the approver in writing before the next close.

causes.title: A long close
causes.text: Ledge reports that half of finance teams take longer than five business days to close. A long close leaves more room for late items to arrive after a month is locked.

fixes.title: Set the closing date and password
fixes.text: Admins set the closing date and password under Settings > Account and settings > Advanced > Accounting. Once it is set, changes to a closed period need the password. It is the main control in QuickBooks Online for stopping accidental reopens.

fixes.title: Run the Exceptions to Closing Date report
fixes.text: Intuit's report lists changes made after the books were closed. Run it at the start of each close and before you sign off. Any line it shows is a reopen you can explain before a client asks.

fixes.title: Save the reports before any undo
fixes.text: Export the reconciliation report, the attachments, and the statement balances for the month before you click Undo. The undo deletes reports and attachments and cannot be reversed. A saved PDF costs nothing.

fixes.title: Reconcile the oldest open month first
fixes.text: A later month depends on the balances that came before it. Work from the oldest open month, and check each one before you move on. An error found early costs less than one found in the next close.

fixes.title: Keep a reopen log
fixes.text: Use a sheet in Excel or Numbers with one row per reopen. Record the month, the account, the reason, who approved it, and the date. After a few months, the log shows which step keeps failing.

fixes.title: Write a short reopen rule
fixes.text: Agree on who approves a reopen, what needs a written reason, and how the client hears about it. Post the rule where the team can find it. A written rule means nobody argues it out during a close.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.title: Confirm the owner
plan.text: Confirm who owns the fix. Check whether you are the Primary Admin, or ask them. Check the closing date setting before you change anything.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.title: Save the evidence
plan.text: Export the reconciliation report, the attachments, and the statement balances for the month. Store the copies only where your firm allows.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.title: Pick the smallest fix
plan.text: Decide between unmarking one line and undoing the whole month. Write the reason in one sentence. A single line is usually the smaller step.

plan.label: Day 4
plan.title: Make the change
plan.text: Make the change in QuickBooks Online using the steps above. Ask Lazur to walk you through each click if the screen looks different from this page.

plan.label: Day 5
plan.title: Reconcile again
plan.text: Reconcile the statement again. Match every line against the bank statement. Confirm the statement balances match the report before you finish.

plan.label: Day 6
plan.title: Check the next month
plan.text: Open the next month and check its beginning balance. Confirm it matches the last statement before you close it.

plan.label: Day 7
plan.title: Lock it and log it
plan.text: Set or review the closing date and run the Exceptions to Closing Date report. Log the cause and the approver, then tell the client what changed.
